`entityLastNameRaw` carries the publisher's own presentation markup — `"Accalia, Jayme
(102162)"` — verbatim. Splitting it into a name is a promotion-step decision that can be checked against the ballot; doing it here would edit a government's record on a guess.

NO PER-ENTITY CYCLE TOTAL IS DERIVED. Several rows share one EntityID with differing Income/Expense and an identical CashBalance. Tested over the population 2026-08-31: sum(Income) - sum(Expense) equals CashBalance for 134 of 255 entities and BREAKS for 121, including single-row entities where there is nothing to sum. Publishing either aggregation as a named person's campaign total would be a wrong figure on a card.

What would settle it: ExportEntityTransactions (itemized, summable), the filed reports, or the ftp://ftp.azsos.gov/cfsdata2/ bulk drop — 8,828 committees, reachable 2026-08-26, and unwalked for this purpose because this process holds no FTP client.

unresolved: THE QUERY IS UNFILTERED BY CYCLE. `filerName: ""` asks the index for everything it holds, so rows carry election years across many cycles and each row states its own `electionYear`. Filtering to one cycle is the promotion step's decision, not a normalizer's — a normalizer that dropped rows would make the staged file smaller than what was acquired.

FILER-LEVEL TOTALS ONLY. The CFS holds contribution and expenditure DETAIL behind endpoints this project has not derived (route nh-cfs-transaction-detail, REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER), so these totals are what the filer reported and are not an itemized record of their money.

NO BALLOT JOIN IS PERFORMED HERE. Matching a filer to a candidacy needs name AND office AND year, plus the county and district guards `lib/funding/state-money.ts` states; that judgement belongs to the promotion step and not to a normalizer.
